reviews.title: Questions, Questions and more Questions
reviews.text:
I saw the add. Wanted to give it a try, but the parade of never-ending questions was a stopper. It was just question after question after question. Let me download the app, launch it and take it from there. 

“What do you want to take photos of?” “Will it be most during the day or at night?” “Will you be taking portraits?” “Are you using this for vacation or home?” “Are you taking photos of your pets?” “How many licks does it take to get to the tootsie roll center of a tootsie roll tootsie pop?”

What I want to know when I launch an app for the first time: subscription price, that’s it. Not a parade of which celebrities are using it and not an endless river of question. Download the app, get the price, decide if it’s worth it and then either pay for the app or delete it. That’s it.

The AI “detects” images that aren’t part of their “community standards” (what community exactly?) and rejects images that get flagged. These “creative” apps use automated censorship without recourse in order to try and scale and extract as much profit as possible at the expense of their users. reviews.title: Credit and Copyright Scam
reviews.text:
After reading the review I downloaded this app and subscribed to a yearly fee. 
First problem:
You can’t use AI filters unless you agree that the images produced using your photos will be passed on and used by other AI Users. I was reluctant to agree but had already subscribed so I continued with caution. As an artist my business relies on my copyright.
Then I uploaded a photo tried out a few premium filters and a pop-up told me I was out of credit and to pay £2.99 for 2 or £20 for 43 more filters (60% off) 
No ONCE did it mention that as well as paying the yearly flat rate that there would also be a credit system on the premium filters.
This was the last straw and I asked Apple for a refund and have now cancelled my account!

reviews.title: Don’t download
reviews.text:
I honestly regret downloading this app. I paid $5 for it expecting at least something useful, functional, and close to what was shown in the advertising. Unfortunately, the actual app is completely different from what is presented in the ads.

The advertising makes this app look amazing and makes it seem like you are getting a useful, high-quality product. But after paying for it and actually using it, I was extremely disappointed. The app barely does what it promises, and the overall experience is frustrating and feels like a complete waste of money.

The interface is confusing, the features are disappointing, and the app simply does not live up to the expectations created by its advertising. It feels like the developers put much more effort into making the advertisement look good than into actually making a good application.

I paid $5 for this, and honestly, even $1 would feel like too much. If I had known what the actual app was like before paying, I would never have downloaded it.

The biggest problem is the misleading advertising. What you see in the advertisement gives you one impression of the app, but the actual product is completely different. That is extremely frustrating, especially when you have already paid for it.

I would strongly recommend NOT downloading this app and definitely not paying for it. Save your money and find another application that actually does what it claims to do.

For me, this was a complete waste of $5 and my time. Very disappointing exper

reviews.title: Greedy, dishonest app that uses AI advertising
reviews.text:
I started using the app to adjust lighting, contrast, etc. to enhance my photos. Once done, it asks me to pay for premium to unlock the effects I just used. However, it never tells you what effects are behind a paywall, so I’m stuck wondering what I can do before I have to start paying for a mobile app. Not only is this really confusing, leaving users playing a guessing game on which assets they’re allowed on the free version; but it’s very greedy. 

After trying to edit my photos, I could not help but notice that they are pushing out AI generated advertisements on Instagram. The pics they use of “models” on their ads aren’t even real. With how many people use this app and pay for the premium, you would think the company would use the examples of its users instead of gallons of water to generate fake people and fake examples. 

The reviews of this app are most likely the result of botting, because the App Store says mostly five stars, but the only positive reviews have come from 6+ years ago before these developers became money hungry. (And lazy by the apparent AI usage). The follow up of the reviews are that they’re a big company trying to pay their staff, but the amount of money they ask for very, VERY limited features won’t justify that. 

Overall, useless app if you’re not paying for it. Limited by the looks of the people that do. Not descriptive of what’s available in general for the standard version. Lazy and sloppy AI content to push its advertising. What a waste of ti

reviews.title: Scam. You paid and still need to buy credits.
reviews.text:
I paid for the yearly Prequel Gold subscription expecting full access to the app’s features, only to discover that I still need to purchase additional credits to edit more photos. This feels incredibly misleading and honestly like a complete scam.

If I’m already paying for a premium annual subscription, I shouldn’t be hit with extra paywalls just to continue using features that appear to be part of the service. The app advertises “unlimited access” to effects and editing tools, yet some features are still locked behind another payment system. (App Store)

I used to enjoy this app, but this experience has been extremely disappointing. If you’re considering paying for the yearly plan, be aware that the subscription may not include everything you expect and that additional credits may still be required. I definitely won’t be renewing unless this policy changes.

reviews.title: AI Erased My Identity: Turned Me Into a White Woman Every Time
reviews.text:
I am extremely disappointed with my experience using the GX7 AI filter on Prequel.

As a Black woman, I uploaded several different photos and, on every single occasion, the AI transformed me into a White woman. My skin tone, facial features, and overall appearance were completely altered, despite it being very clear from the original images that I am Black.

AI filters are meant to enhance or creatively transform images, not erase a person’s ethnicity or fundamentally change their racial identity. The fact that this happened repeatedly across multiple attempts suggests there may be significant bias within the AI’s training data or image-generation process.

Representation and inclusivity matter. No user should feel that their natural features are being ignored or replaced because they do not fit a default standard. I hope the developers take this feedback seriously and work towards improving the diversity and accuracy of their AI models so that all users are represented fairly.

Until these issues are addressed, I cannot recommend this feature.

reviews.title: Misleading Subscription and Hidden Credit System
reviews.text:
Very misleading subscription model. I paid for a YEARLY subscription mainly because of the AI “golden hour” photo effects, only to discover after editing just a few photos that I suddenly needed to buy additional credits to continue using the feature.

Nowhere during the subscription purchase was it clearly explained that the main AI tools are heavily limited and locked behind extra credit payments. Selling a yearly subscription while hiding essential usage limits is deceptive and extremely disappointing.

I cancelled immediately and requested a refund. Be careful before paying — the subscription does NOT give you unlimited access to the features they advertise.

reviews.title: Not worth it
reviews.text: I’m trying to understand what the benefit of this app’s 3-day trial is. I appreciate any app with paid features that allows a temporary trial period to see if this works for them or not. They hooked me based on some pretty cool lighting effect photo editing features that I wanted to try. When opening the app for the first time, I’m met with a ton of other filters and thought I’d play with those to see what they do. Some photos worked really well and others not so much. So after a few failed attempts with bad photo selections on my part, I rounded up a handful of good photos I wanted to apply the lighting filters to. However, on my first attempt I was met with a blocker alert, saying that I’ve used up all of my 10 uses and it won’t reset for 7 days. 7 days???? My trial end ends in 3 days! What was the point? I didn’t download and subscribe to this app’s trial for photo editing features already built-in on my phone. I didn’t even get to test the one filter I downloaded this app for. There’s no way I can justify paying for this service and already deleted from my phone. I’m sure the app is great for those who pay for it, but I feel like this is such a bait and switch. It took me all of two minutes to use up my 7 day limit to use the features I downloaded the app for. I’ll never go back to this app again.

reviews.title: Lack of Transparency About AI Limits in Gold Subscription
reviews.text:
I purchased the Gold subscription for the Prequel iPhone app expecting full access to the features, especially the holiday templates. Unfortunately, despite having an active paid subscription, I cannot use any festive templates because I supposedly reached an AI usage limit.

What is most frustrating is that:
	•	There is no clear information about any AI limits before purchasing the subscription.
	•	The app keeps telling me to “come back later,” and I have been seeing this message for three days in a row.
	•	As a paying user, I feel misled — this looks like a very unclear and unfair marketing policy.

I would like to ask the developers:
	•	What exactly is the AI limit for Gold subscribers?
	•	Why is this information not disclosed upfront before buying the subscription?
	•	How long am I actually supposed to wait to regain access?

Paying for a premium plan but being blocked from advertised features is unacceptable. Until this policy is transparent and fixed, I cannot recommend this app.
